question: What is the difference between `free()` and `delete`?

scenes.sub: delete destroys the object first. free only returns bytes.
scenes.say: free versus delete. Both give memory back to the heap. But only delete knows there was an object living in it.

scenes.head: delete = destructor + deallocation
scenes.say: A Doc holds a string. new builds the Doc, and its string allocates a separate heap buffer, for a hundred characters. Now delete d. First it runs the destructor, so the string frees its buffer. Then it releases the Doc's own memory. free would skip step one entirely. It's a plain C function that knows nothing about destructors. And calling free on memory from new isn't just a leak. It's undefined behavior.

scenes.head: Mixing them up
scenes.say: All of these are undefined behavior. new with free. malloc with delete. And new square brackets with plain delete. They might seem to work for an int, but the standard makes no promise, and with real classes they break. One thing they share: deleting null p t r, or freeing a null pointer, safely does nothing. So you never need an if check before delete.

scenes.head: Side by side
scenes.say: free is a C library function, delete is an operator. Destructor: free never calls it, delete calls it first. Memory source: free only takes memory from malloc, calloc or realloc. delete only takes memory from new. Arrays: free doesn't care, but delete needs the square bracket form for arrays. Null: both are safe no ops. And only delete can be customized, by overloading operator delete.

lines: delete runs the destructor, then releases memory. free only releases bytes.
Pair them: malloc → free, new → delete, new[] → delete[]. Mixing is UB.
Both are no-ops on a null pointer. Best of all: let smart pointers delete.
scenes.say: delete runs the destructor, then releases the memory. free only releases bytes. Always pair them: malloc with free, new with delete, new square brackets with delete square brackets. Both are safe on a null pointer. And best of all, let a smart pointer call delete for you.
